name: Tacit Labs
summary: Tacit develops AI-assisted underwriting intelligence for MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders, recovering judgement embedded in prior pricing and risk decisions.
overview: Tacit develops underwriting intelligence for MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders. Its platform is designed to recover the judgment embedded in historical pricing and risk decisions, then make that context available in future underwriting workflows.

bull_case: If Tacit can turn fragmented underwriting history into a trusted workflow layer, it can benefit from deep integration, proprietary customer data and recurring insurance-software spend.
bear_case: Insurance buyers require accuracy, explainability and regulatory discipline. The company has not publicly disclosed financing, valuation or commercial metrics, so its progress is difficult to independently assess.

intelligence.description: Underwriting-intelligence platform for MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders.
company: Tacit develops underwriting intelligence for MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders. It focuses on retrieving the judgment embedded in prior technical pricing and risk decisions so underwriters can use that context in future cases.
The company has not publicly disclosed financing, valuation or operating metrics. This profile therefore assesses the product category and does not infer a transaction or commercial scale.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Insurance underwriting depends on institutional knowledge that is often poorly captured across spreadsheets and systems. A product that makes that judgment accessible and auditable could be valuable, but adoption depends on accuracy, explainability and trust.

changed.text: Tacit’s public materials state that it is raising pre-seed; no completed-round amount or valuation is disclosed.

takeaways: Tacit targets technical pricing and underwriting workflows for MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders.
Its premise is that historical underwriting judgment can be made usable in future decisions.
No public valuation is asserted without a confirmed priced transaction.
The next useful evidence will be product adoption, financing, and operating disclosure.
